title: Claim Acceptance Standards: Home Protection Plans
content:
These standards decide whether a repair claim under any of the Home Protection Plans is accepted and approved, and the outcome recorded when it is denied. A claim concerns one failure of one covered system.

## 1. Conditions of approval

1.1 A claim is approved only for a covered system of the plan whose failure date is on or after the coverage start date.

1.2 Claims are approved only while the plan is active. The plan's status is read from the company's plan record before the claim is decided; a plan in waiting period or cancelled is not active.

1.3 A claim is accepted only when the customer files it no later than the plan's claim filing deadline, in calendar days, after the failure occurred. Day one is the calendar day after the failure date, and the filing window closes at the end of the calendar day equal to the failure date plus the filing deadline in days; a claim filed on that last day is in time. The failure date is the date of the failure as diagnosed by the network contractor and recorded on the claim; the filing date is the day the customer files the claim. The filing deadline is 30 calendar days for every plan in the line.

## 2. Denial outcomes

| Finding | Recorded outcome |
|---|---|
| The failure is dated before the coverage start date | Denied: waiting period |
| The contractor finds the condition pre-existing, and the plan excludes pre-existing conditions | Denied: pre-existing |
| The equipment is older than the plan's equipment age limit at the failure date, and that limit is above 0 | Denied: not covered |
| The plan year's repair count had already reached the plan's maximum covered repairs per plan year when the claim was made | Denied: cap reached |

## 3. Plan year and repair count

The plan year for a claim is the plan year containing the failure date, counted from an anniversary of the coverage start date to the day before the next anniversary. The plan year's repair count is the number of approved claims on the plan in that plan year whose claim type is repair, replacement or surge electronics, leaving out return visits that name an earlier claim as the claim they repeat. Tune-up claims are not of those types and so are not counted.

## 4. Boundary cases (hypothetical dates and figures)

**Filing window.** Failure dated 4 June; filing deadline 30 days. Day one is 5 June and the window closes at the end of 4 July.
- Filed 4 July: in time.
- Filed 5 July: not accepted.

**Coverage start.** Coverage start date 9 April.
- Failure dated 9 April: on the coverage start date, so the waiting period ground does not apply.
- Failure dated 8 April: denied, waiting period.

**Repair count.** A plan allows 3 covered repairs per plan year. In the current plan year it has two approved repairs, one approved return visit naming one of them, and one approved tune-up. The repair count is 2, below 3, so the cap reached ground does not apply to a new repair claim in that plan year. Had there been three approved repairs, the new claim would be denied, cap reached.

**Equipment age.** A plan's equipment age limit is 15 years. A unit manufactured 25 years before the failure date is older than the limit: denied, not covered. Under a plan whose limit is 0, equipment age is never a ground of denial.
